historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR diverges >30% from revenue/EPS: the '5yr' columns are 4-year FY2021-FY2025 spans (history starts FY2021), and the Jan-2023 spin-off recapitalised the balance sheet (equity $16.7B -> $9.4B, $10.2B debt assumed), so equity and EPS CAGRs measure the separation, not the business. Revenue CAGR is the anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less net-share-settlement taxes): FY2022 1,757 / FY2023 1,567 / FY2024 1,336 / FY2025 1,333 (USD m). The -8.8% owner-FCF CAGR vs -6.2% reported is SBC growing ($67M -> $172M incl. withholding) faster than cash flow; the bulk of the decline is the post-spin interest burden (~$350M/yr after tax from FY2023) and pension contributions, not operations. Reported FCF plus after-tax interest is roughly flat at ~$1.8-1.85B across FY2022-FY2025.

scenario_narratives.base: GEHC remains one of the three global imaging incumbents growing with hospital capex: organic 3-4% in FY2026 lifts to ~4.5% in FY2027 as the largest launch cycle in a decade (SIGNA Sprint/Bolt/One MRI, photon-counting and True Definition CT, MIM AI contouring) converts from a record $23.9B backlog, Intelerad adds a cloud enterprise-imaging layer, and PDx radiopharmaceuticals grow faster than the group. China stays flat rather than recovering. Tariffs settle at roughly neutral after USMCA and US-manufacturing mitigation; the Section 232 probe produces no large new duty. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin dips to 16.5% in FY2026 on input inflation and integration costs then expands ~15bps/yr to 18% -- less than a third of management's adjusted-margin ambition. Growth fades to 2.5% by FY2034 and the terminal multiple is capped at 16x owner FCF. The pension deficit and net debt are deducted at the Q2 2026 balance sheet.
scenario_narratives.bull: The launch cycle takes share from Siemens Healthineers and Philips in MRI and CT, pricing holds as photon-counting and Deep Silicon detectors move GEHC into premium tiers, the software/AI attach rate on the installed base (CareIntellect, Intelerad, MIM) lifts recurring mix, and China stabilises after the anti-corruption procurement freeze. Revenue grows 5-7% through FY2029 and the pre-SBC EBITDA margin reaches 20% by FY2033 (management's ~50bps/yr adjusted goal, delivered). Tariffs turn into a net positive as USMCA-certified US production displaces imports. Terminal growth 3% with an 18x cap -- still below the multiple Siemens Healthineers commands.
scenario_narratives.bear: A Section 232 finding imposes new duties on imaging components and the US-China tariff truce unwinds, so the FY2026 tariff headwind returns; memory-chip and freight inflation persists; China revenue keeps shrinking as United Imaging and Mindray move upmarket and win export tenders; hospital capex slows with rates. Revenue growth stalls at 1.5-2% after the Intelerad lap and the pre-SBC EBITDA margin compresses to 15% and stays there. With ~$10B of debt, a $5B pension deficit and a 13x terminal cap, the equity is a thin slice of enterprise value and the bear value falls to roughly two-thirds of the current price.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the consolidated operating business on unlevered, SBC-expensed owner FCF built from components, discount at an 8% USD WACC held constant across scenarios, cap the terminal value at 13-18x owner FCF, then deduct net debt at the 2026-06-30 balance sheet, the after-tax pension deficit and the minority share once each. The result is compared with the current price on a probability-weighted basis and against a 15% hurdle entry price. Because interest and the pension are charged through WACC and the bridge, the projected flows are ~$0.9B/yr above the FCF the company reports; the reconciliation to the ~$1.6B FY2026 FCF guide is stated in inputs.notes.
key_risks_to_valuation: Section 232 medical-equipment tariff investigation (opened Sept 2026) could re-impose the ~$500M gross headwind that mitigation removed in 2026
China (~13% of revenue) is flat-to-down with local competitors gaining; the base case assumes no recovery but also no further collapse
Pension deficit ($5.2B) is rate-sensitive; a 100bps fall in discount rates raises it and the bridge deduction by roughly $2B
Leverage: $10.1B debt after the debt-funded $2.3B Intelerad deal; equity is only ~70% of EV, so a 10% change in EV moves the per-share value ~14%
Margin path assumes launch-cycle pricing and mix offset input-cost inflation; FY2026 already absorbed ~$250M of unexpected inflation
Terminal value is ~55-60% of EV even with the multiple cap; the sensitivity grid shows the WACC and terminal-growth exposure

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 451.686M cover-page shares at 2026-07-22 (Q2 2026 10-Q) plus ~1.3M dilutive RSU/PSU/option equivalents (Q2 2026 diluted weighted average 454M vs basic 453M). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count. Buybacks ($200M FY2025, $300M H1 2026) exceed SBC, so the flat count is funded, not a modelling convention.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: share-based compensation add-back $130M plus taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards $42M (financing). GEHC publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. H1 2026 run-rate is higher ($80M add-back, 0.77% of revenue) after Intelerad.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $200M (cash paid, financing activities); H1 2026 $300M. Dividends $64M FY2025 ($0.14/share).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:01Z regular close (Friday; Monday 2026-09-28 session not yet printed at build time)
inputs.balance_sheet_source: Q2 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-07-29, accession 0001932393-26-000046), read directly from the iXBRL; the Metrics CSV and DuckDB stop at Q1 2026 and were not edited.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 -> cost of equity ~9.2%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.4% ($440M interest on ~$10.1B), ~3.5% after tax. Market weights: equity ~$30B, debt $10.1B plus ~$5.2B debt-like pension -> ~30% debt-like. Blended ~7.7%; rounded to 8.0% for the capital-equipment cyclicality and China exposure. The SAME 8.0% is used in all three scenarios: risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not stacked into per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Operating lease cost stays inside EBITDA as US GAAP operating expense (~$150M/yr cash rent); the $394M operating lease liability (2026-06-30) is therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases (~$42M) are immaterial and sit inside total_debt if tagged there; not separately adjusted.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are modelled on consolidated EBITDA, so the minority share is deducted once in the equity bridge: redeemable NCI ($229M) + NCI ($14M) are carried at book $243M, but NCI took $70M of FY2025 net income (3.2%), so the bridge deducts $910M = 13x that share (roughly the group's own P/E). Not also stripped from the flows.
inputs.pension_treatment: Unfunded pension and OPEB of $5,186M (2026-06-30, PensionAndOtherPostretirementDefinedBenefitPlansLiabilitiesNoncurrent) inherited from GE is a debt-like claim. Service cost is inside operating income (so inside the projected flows); the non-operating pension benefit income (~$288M FY2025, largely non-cash expected-return-on-assets) is OUTSIDE operating income and is NOT in the flows. Cash contributions that fund the deficit (~$350M/yr expected) are NOT deducted from the projected flows; instead the after-tax deficit, $5,186M x (1-21%) = $4,097M, is deducted once in the equity bridge. The alternative -- PV of excess contributions -- would be ~$2.5-3B, so this is the more conservative of the two.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1: operating company). GEHC is a big-three imaging/diagnostics medtech, ~50% recurring revenue, profitable, moderately cyclical -- no adaptations file needed beyond the pension/NCI/lease items stated above. FRESH build (no prior DCF or memory entry). last_fcf ($1,333M) is LEVERED owner FCF as the company reports it: after ~$440M interest (~$350M after tax) and after ~$330M cash pension contributions. The component projection is UNLEVERED and pre-deficit-funding (year-1 ~$2.25B), because interest is charged through WACC and the pension deficit through the bridge; $2.25B less ~$350M after-tax interest less ~$250M excess pension funding is ~$1.65B, which ties to management's FY2026 FCF guide of ~$1.6B. History is short (spun from GE Jan 2023): FY2021-22 carve-out financials carry no debt, so the FCF and equity CAGRs largely measure the spin recapitalisation rather than the business. EBITDA basis: GAAP operating income + depreciation + intangible amortisation + SBC (i.e. pre-SBC, but AFTER restructuring, acquisition and integration costs, which recur every year at GEHC); FY2025 = 2,763+287+291+130 = $3,471M = 16.8%. Management's adjusted EBIT margin (15.4-15.7% FY2026 guide) excludes amortisation and restructuring; reconciles to ~13.3% GAAP operating margin, consistent with the 16.5% pre-SBC EBITDA used for FY2026. Interest income: none deducted -- the company is a net debtor (net debt ~6x owner FCF), so the cash pile is not counted twice.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +6.0% reported = 3.5% organic (guide 3-4%, reaffirmed Q2) + ~2% Intelerad (closed Mar-2026) + FX; H1 2026 printed +6.6%. FY2027 4.5% as the nine 2026 launches convert against a $23.9B backlog (book-to-bill 1.15x), then fading to the ~2.5% terminal rate: the imaging oligopoly grows mid-single digits and China (~13%) is flat.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA 16.8% FY2025 -> 16.5% FY2026 (tariffs, memory/freight inflation ~$250M gross, Intelerad integration costs; guide is 10-40bps adj-EBIT expansion but GAAP absorbs deal costs) -> +120bps over the decade to 18.0% from PDx/software/service mix and launch-cycle pricing; management's ~50bps/yr adjusted ambition, haircut by more than half.
base.capex_da_rationale: Capex 2.3% FY2025, 2.7% H1 2026 (US manufacturing shifts for tariff mitigation) -> 2.6% then 2.5%. D&A 2.8% FY2025, 3.0% H1 2026 with Intelerad intangibles; legacy amortisation ($291M) runs off so D&A converges toward capex by year 10.
base.tax_rationale: Unlevered cash tax on EBIT = cash taxes paid + interest tax shield: FY2023 24%, FY2024 23%, FY2025 19% (interest carryforward DTA used). Path 20% -> 22%, the three-year average.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer with receivables + inventory > payables + customer deposits: growth consumes ~5% of the revenue increase. Deferred revenue rose $81M in FY2025 on $953M of revenue growth, partially offsetting inventory build.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: three live, correlated overhangs (the September 2026 Section 232 medical-equipment tariff investigation, a China business with no recovery catalyst, and $10B debt plus a $5B pension deficit that leave equity ~70% of EV) and a guidance cut already delivered in Q1 2026. Bull cut to 25%: it needs launch-cycle share gains, tariff neutrality AND China stabilisation to all hold at once, plus a margin trajectory the company has not yet demonstrated post-spin (adjusted EBIT margin has expanded ~30bps/yr, not 50).

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
